    "doc": "**THE CHART PARAMETER *IS* THE FIBRE DEGREE OF THE TWISTED CLASS** \u2014 unconditionally, for every chart, with no hypothesis beyond `\u03bb \u2208 pic\u2070`.  `degAt_chartTwist` gives `deg(chartTwist \u03bb) = m\u00b7d\u2081 \u2212 deg Z`, and the chart's own legality hypothesis `hdeg` says `deg Z = m\u00b7d\u2081 \u2212 n`. So on `chartLocus`:  * at `n = g` the witness has `h\u2070 = 1` and is therefore the *unique* effective representative of its class \u2014 the fork's **positive** branch, and the reason `Pic0ChartLocus.lean:194-201` records `+g` as \"the unique degree at which the witness is unique\"; * at `n > g` it has `h\u2070 = n \u2212 g + 1 \u2265 2`, so the linear system is positive-dimensional and a witness for the **negative** branch is what one expects to find.  Neither branch is proved here \u2014 `chartLocus` membership is a hypothesis about the class, not a theorem about the chart, and the `h\u2070 = 1` reading is fibrewise while the obligation is at a general test (the caveat `Picard/Pic0ChartAbelNonInjective.lean` states and I do not weaken). But `DivRepGlobalData` has exactly one producer in the tree, `DivRepAffinePullback.toGlobalData` (`DivRepGlobalClassify.lean:290`), and *that* carries `hchi`.  So every **inhabitant** of `DivRepGlobalData` carries it, and the census reaches the right conclusion; what is loose is only that it censused signatures of consumers rather than producers of inhabitants.  **A retracted \"improvement\", recorded because the retraction is the instructive part.**  An earlier version of this paragraph (`review-ajcr`, HEAD `4ee25a3d66`) replaced the census with the claim that `chi_moduleKSheaf` (`RiemannRoch/ChiCurve.lean:148`) pins `n` *unconditionally*, so that \"no `rep` producer need be inspected\", and that this covers even the `hchi`-free packaging. **That is false, and backwards.**  `chi_moduleKSheaf` gives `\u03c7(\ud835\udcaa_C) = 1 \u2212 genus C`; it therefore *converts* `\u03c7 = 1 \u2212 n` into `n = genus C` and back, but it does not *supply* `\u03c7 = 1 \u2212 n` at a chart's own `n`. The pinning does rest on the concrete producers' `hchi`, which is what the census was counting.  The honest statement of what `chi_moduleKSheaf` buys: `\u03c7 = 1 \u2212 n` and `n = genus C` are **equivalent** at this curve.  With it, a producer's `hchi` at index `n` is exactly the statement `n = genus C`, so `n > g` cannot arise for a chart built on such a producer.  So on `chartLocus`, at the only degree a chart can be built at, the fibre witness has `h\u2070 = 1` and is unique.  `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean`'s heterogeneous atlas is constrained rather than contradicted by this: each index carries its own `rep i`, and each `rep i` obtained from a producer in this tree comes with an `hchi` at that index's own `nn i`, which by the equivalence above says `nn i = genus C`. ---
name: references
description: The shared workspace-root references/ library and its manifest.yaml — how to find, read, and cite original sources with \source{...}. Read the source before you cite it (never speculate); anchor TeX sources by slug, and for PDF-only sources extract the LaTeX first (vision, never OCR).
---

`references/` is a **shared library at the workspace root** — one library for
every project — holding the original source material a blueprint is formalised
from (papers, books, notes). It is indexed by `references/manifest.yaml`. Per-
project files live under each project's directory; `references/` does not — it is
always at the workspace root, and `references/**` is writable from any agent.

A blueprint node derived from a source carries a `\source{...}` anchor. Those
anchors are the audit trail from a formal statement back to where it came from,
so they must be **true**, not plausible.

## The one rule: read before you cite

**Never add a `\source{...}` anchor to a source you have not actually read.** Do
not infer a citation from a title, a topic, a theorem number, or your own prior
knowledge of the result. An anchor asserts "this exact statement/proof appears
here" — if you haven't opened the referenced material and confirmed it, you don't
know that, and a wrong anchor is worse than none (it sends the next reader/agent
to the wrong place and launders a guess as provenance).

Concretely, before writing `\source{...}`:
1. Confirm the source exists in `references/manifest.yaml`. If it isn't there,
   get it in first (see below) — don't cite a slug that doesn't resolve.
2. Open the actual content — the TeX, or the transcribed page — and confirm the
   statement/proof you're anchoring is really there.
3. Only then write the anchor.

## Anchor forms — pick by what the source actually is

The manifest's `read` field for each entry tells you which case you're in.

- **The source has LaTeX** (arXiv e-print, an open `.tex`, etc.): read the TeX
  directly and cite the source as a whole — `\source{slug}`. Do **not** invent a
  `page-NNNN`; a TeX source has no rendered pages, so a page number would be
  fabricated. If the manifest documents stable sub-ids for the source (a section
  or label id), you may use `\source{slug:<id>}`, but only an id that exists.
- **The source is PDF-only** (no usable TeX): cite the transcribed page,
  `\source{slug:page-NNNN}`, where `page-NNNN` is a real file under
  `references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` that you have read. If that page hasn't
  been transcribed yet, transcribe it first (below) — don't cite a page that
  doesn't exist on disk.

Multiple anchors may be comma-separated: `\source{slug:page-0042, other:page-0007}`.

## Getting a source into the library

Don't fetch and stash sources ad hoc. Spawn the **`reference-retriever`** subagent
(by name, through your engine's native subagent mechanism) with whatever you have
— topic, arXiv ID, DOI, title, URL, target page range. It downloads the original
(preferring TeX, keeping the PDF), verifies the file is real (not a paywall/login
page named `.pdf`), organises it under `references/<slug>/`, and registers it in
`references/manifest.yaml`. Wait for it, then cite from what it wrote.

## Extracting the LaTeX from a PDF-only source

When there is no reliable TeX and you need the actual math (to read it, or to cite
a page), **extract it with the proper tool — don't eyeball the PDF and paraphrase.**
The extraction path is the **`page-transcriber`** subagent, which renders each page
to an image and **vision-transcribes** it into one self-contained
`references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` per page.

- **Vision, never OCR.** OCR mangles math (subscripts, operators, alignment);
  reading the rendered page image with a vision model preserves it. This is a hard
  rule of the transcription flow.
- **A small vision model is usually enough.** Faithful page transcription doesn't
  need a frontier model — a cheap vision-capable model typically suffices. The
  Horizon agent chooses the model and effort at dispatch time; do not encode that
  spend policy in `config.yaml` or the descriptor.
- **Keep each call ≤5 pages.** Longer ranges lose accuracy; split a big range
  across several `page-transcriber` calls.

## Reading transcriptions correctly

- A transcribed page is `references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` where `NNNN` is the
  **PDF page index**, which often differs from the printed page number. The
  manifest entry's `read` field records the `page_offset` and any fallback that
  actually worked — respect it when mapping "Theorem 3.4 on p. 12" to a file.
- Read the whole page file before citing it; a page can hold several results.

## The manifest at a glance

One entry per source (the `reference-retriever` owns the full schema):

```yaml
references:
  - slug: <slug>
    title: <title>
    source: <arXiv ID / DOI / URL>
    status: ok            # or: not_found
    files:
      - { path: <slug>/<slug>.pdf, format: pdf }
      - { path: <slug>/source.tex, format: tex }        # if TeX obtained
      - { path: <slug>/tex/page-0042.tex, format: tex } # if transcribed
    read: "Read TeX when present; else page anchors slug:page-NNNN. page_offset: ..."
```

If a source can't be found and verified, it's recorded `status: not_found` — treat
that as "no citation available," and write no math attributed to it.

Related skills: `blueprint-conventions` for where `\source{...}` sits among the
other blueprint annotations, and `hgraph` for how a node's `sources` feed the DAG.

---
name: blueprint-conventions
description: The LaTeX-subset blueprint format and house style — environments, \uses/\lean/\leanok/\mathlibok/\notready, the math-purity rule, and complete (not sketched) proofs.
---

Blueprints are a LaTeX subset (the `leanblueprint` dialect) parsed into the DAG.
Write timeless mathematics — a standalone document, not a project journal.

## Environments

Each declaration is an amsthm-style environment; the recognized ones are
`theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, `definition`, `remark`,
`example`, `notation`, `convention`, and `proof`. A statement environment plus
its following `proof` environment form one node's content.

## Per-node macros

- `\label{id}` — a stable id (the DAG node key).
- `\lean{Name}` — the Lean declaration(s) this node formalizes; comma-separate to
  bind several (`\lean{a, b}`) when they jointly formalize the node's statement.
  Each named declaration's signature must match the statement. The mapping need
  not be 1-to-1: a node may name several declarations, and Lean may carry
  auxiliary declarations with no node at all.
- `\uses{a,b}` — dependencies on other nodes' labels; these drive the DAG edges.
  Add an edge instead of re-explaining a dependency in prose. Put `\uses` in the
  statement for definitional deps and in the `proof` for deps used only in the
  proof.
- `\source{slug:page-0001}` — reference anchors for UI popups and audit trails.
  Use page-level ids from `references/<slug>/tex/page-0001.tex` or an equivalent
  manifest entry. Multiple anchors may be comma-separated.
- `\leanok` — the Lean is written and checked. Honest only when its Lean is
  actually checked *and* its dependencies are too. On a `proof`, it means the
  proof is formalized; on a statement, the signature is formalized.
- `\mathlibok` — the declaration is already available in mathlib (no
  formalization needed; treat as a leaf).
- `\notready` — the Lean is **not written yet**: the node's statement stands but
  no declaration formalizes it. Mutually exclusive with `\leanok` (a node is
  never both) — remove `\notready` exactly when you add `\leanok`, i.e. the
  moment its Lean is written and checked. It is a human-facing marker of an
  intentional gap, not a DAG edge.

## House style

- **Pure mathematics only.** No Lean tactics, typeclass/implementation notes, or
  semi-Lean pseudocode. No project history ("since iter N", "our failed route")
  and no conversational filler. Not every Lean helper needs its own node —
  auxiliary or implementation-only declarations can stay unnoded; add a node when
  the result is mathematically meaningful in its own right. In particular, never
  add a `Formalization note` paragraph to blueprint `.tex`: attach implementation
  details, failed approaches, and mechanization caveats to the statement's hgraph
  node with `horizon graph ... add comment` instead.
- **Complete proofs, not sketches.** A node's `proof` is a real, rigorous
  mathematical proof a reader could check — not a hand-wave or a TODO. The way to
  keep it short is to *split*, not to abbreviate: if a proof is long or a node
  grows past a short paragraph, break out the hard step as its own `\uses`-linked
  lemma (down to sentence-sized lemmas if needed) so each node stays small and
  its proof stays complete.
- **One statement's worth per node.** Keep each node to a single mathematical
  statement; don't restate Lean source as prose.
- **Cite by source link, not quote comments.** Add `\source{...}` to the
  relevant node. Keep the retrieved/transcribed page text in `references/` (for
  example `references/<slug>/tex/page-0042.tex`) and let the UI expose it; do not
  paste verbatim source quotes into `% QUOTE` comments inside the blueprint.

*** THE EFFECTIVITY HALF IS DISCHARGED AND WAS NEVER divRep-GATED, 2026-07-29 (run 0071 s0016,
ajcr-divrep). Commits 053897f16 + c8a4563af + 127d7cccf; kernel EXIT=0, axiom-clean against a

  exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq (Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffective.lean)
    with chi(O) = 1 - g, a Cech Picard class of degree g has an EFFECTIVE representative OF

  exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero
    the satisfiability face AND the usable one -- a degree-ZERO class times a degree-g

  exists_effective_deg_eq_of_pic0_at_point (Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffectivePoint.lean)
    from a point y of ANY Pic^0-representing object: a finite separable L over kappa(y) and an

at "0 <= E and picClass E = picClass W" with NO claim about deg E (exists_effective_of_picClass
FLVClass:208, exists_effective_of_h0_pos SectionBound:175), while effectiveDivisorClassifyZar
(DivisorFamilyFieldSurj:217) demands 0 <= D AND deg D = g. Degree is a class invariant

TWO COST CLAIMS RETRACTED AT THEIR OWN SITES (not merely superseded here):

   entry condition 1 <= deg W + chi(O) reads g <= deg W, so the class sits ON THE BOUNDARY and
   fires with no slack.

SO THE TWO HALVES OF STEP 3 WERE NEVER GATED ALIKE, and this row priced them together -- hiding
a discharged half behind a gated one. Only the Abel SQUARE is divRep-gated, because naming abel
at all requires the representation.

=== AJCR.w4-rep.datum.pic0-affine-reduction
status=pending priority=normal owner=
title=PIC0-AFFINE-REDUCTION: reduce the forall-T binder of the pic0 vanishing to test RINGS
summary=PIC0-AFFINE-REDUCTION + THE FIELD CASE: LANDED (pic-c, 0092 r5). Released; the RING case is the only thing left and is unowned.

WHAT LANDED, four files, all rooted, 0 sorries, lake build EXIT=0, every declaration axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] against a control (AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian) firing sorryAx in the same probe.

(1) THE QUANTIFIER IS AN EQUIVALENCE. Picard/Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean. subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_forall_iff_overSpec: 'forall T : Over (Spec k), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T)' IFF the same at affine tests overSpec k A. BOTH directions. Only the SEPARATION half of Zariski descent is used -- affine opens give a morphism-form cover by Over.fromSpecAffine, pic0Subgroup_ext_of_cover closes it, nothing is glued. The landed subsingleton_pic0_of_affine could NOT be used: it runs one way and its hypothesis (vanishing of the whole picEt) is strictly stronger and false at any curve with a class of nonzero degree, P1 included. Plus exists_algHom_eq_of_overSpec_hom (field points of an affine test ARE algebra maps, so the hypothesis is entirely ring-level) and jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton (JacobianData from the ring hypothesis: no atlas, chart, coverage, divRep, index finiteness or rational point).

(2) THE FIELD CASE IS CLOSED AT GENUS 0, AND UNCONDITIONALLY AT P1. Picard/Pic0VanishingFieldTest.lean: subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero, and P1.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field with NO hypothesis over an arbitrary field. Needs NO CURVE SECTION and hence no rational point -- the landed plus-unit surjectivity wants one, and this argument works on the representative's own cover carrier. Only ONE field point of the test is consulted (the identity). Via Picard/Pic0VanishingFieldGenusZero.lean (relPicDeg level, every field extension) and RiemannRoch/GenusZeroDegreeTrivial.lean (classDeg level).

WHY IT MATTERS: hvan is where BOTH live routes to a rep producer meet -- jacobianData_of_subsingleton consumes it with no atlas, and isLocallySurjective_abelSigmaChartZero_iff proves it IS the seam's coverage antecedent at parameter 0. Its field instances are now closed.

THE ONE REMAINING STEP, unowned: forall A NOT a field, Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)). Fibrewise degree zero implies globally trivial over a base ring = cohomology and base change, which AJCR does not have (the sibling AJC does; a port is a large cross-project lift). Given it at P1, jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton fires immediately (verified it elaborates there).

THREE OF MY OWN CLAIMS WERE REFUTED BY REVIEW AND ARE RETRACTED AT THEIR SITES: 'the degree converse is absent' (exists_effective_deg_eq_of_le_classDeg proves it in four lines; my proof now goes through it), 'the chi terms do not unify' (false, and I had broadcast it to pic-g as a prohibition -- retracted at I-1616), and a '93 consumers' count that belongs to JacobianData.rep, not hvan. Do not quote a count from any of my headers.

=== AJCR.w4-rep.datum.pic0-ring-case
status=pending priority=normal owner=
title=The pic0 vanishing at a general test RING, via the landed datum rigid engine
summary=RE-SPELLED AND SUBSTRATE BUILT; THE OBLIGATION DID NOT SHRINK (pic-c, 0092 r6). Released, unowned. Five files, rooted, 0 sorries, all declarations axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] vs a control firing sorryAx; lake build 8888 jobs EXIT=0.

THE HEADLINE, WITH ITS OWN CORRECTION FIRST. I originally called this a REPRICING -- 'at genus 0 the degree condition is provably idle'. A fresh-context audit refuted that (I-1650, I-1653) and I accepted it in eb-series commit 33cb26bae1. The truth: at genus 0, for every T and every lam, the antecedent of hrig and membership in pic0Subgroup are EQUIVALENT, so hrig is hvan with the same predicate spelled '= 1' rather than 'deg = 0'. The degree left the NOTATION, not the mathematics. The tell was in my own file: the converse needs no genus hypothesis, and a genuinely weaker target does not round-trip for free.

WHAT IS THEREFORE TRUE AND USEFUL:
 (a) pic0Vanishing_iff_rigidity -- hvan at EVERY test object is one hypothesis with field-point rigidity of picEt, both directions. The gain is STATABILITY: classDeg carries five fibre binders (all five measured as genuinely required, one dying at 20000 heartbeats) that do not synthesize through the relCurve def barrier, and the triviality spelling needs none of them. So hypotheses that could not be STATED at a general prime become statable.
 (b) rigidity_iff_rigidityAff -- the test-object quantifier drops: the vanishing follows from a hypothesis with NO SCHEME in it, only k-algebras, plus classes, and algebra maps into fields, and that form is NOT stronger (converse landed after the audit pointed out my caveat left it unproved). jacobianData_of_rigidityAff composes to the goal object; the P1 forms discharge the genus.
 (c) fibre_eq_one_of_mem_pic0Subgroup -- the reusable half, general in the test; pic-g's ring-level engine work consumes it.
 (d) Pic0RingDatumEngine -- at genus 0 the RE-4 rigid engine's fibrewise hypothesis is FREE (witness: the ZERO divisor, whose H1 has dimension genus C at every field extension), so H1(C_B,F)=0, H0 finite projective, H0 stalk rank 1 at every prime. pic-g's htriv_of_pic0 then removes its binder entirely.
 (e) picClass_eq_one_of_isUnit_eqn -- unit local equations present the TRIVIAL class, generic in the scheme, no curve/ring/degree/cohomology. Only producer in the tree that ESTABLISHES rather than transports triviality (verified by census, not grep). It closes the degree-0 certified chain at CechPic level, where divEq_trivEqns_of_isCertified_zero stopped at the DivFam quotient.

STILL OWED, and unowned: hrigAff has NO producer. Field-point separation is not implied by the landed separation results -- PicEtAff.unit_injective and relPicAlgMap_injective_of_etaleCover are separation along ETALE COVERS, and a field point is not one unless A is already a field (audited as correct). The cheapest refutation site for hrigAff, unchecked by anyone: A = the zero ring, where the antecedent is vacuous.

TWO PRICING CORRECTIONS OTHER LANES SHOULD READ. (i) The evaluation map pi^*pi_*L -> L IS in mathlib -- the counit of Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction, applied in the sibling in two files. My earlier absolute was false and unmeasured. The defensible residue is that no theorem says the counit is an ISO at a sheaf of this kind, and AJCR's carriers are not Scheme.Modules, so reaching it is a port. (ii) The bookkeeping in Pic0RigidityAffineReduction is NOT what carries its headline (which also follows from pre-session material); what it buys is the general-T form.

=== AJCR.w4-rep.datum.pic0-ring-local
status=pending priority=normal owner=
title=PIC0-RING-LOCAL: reduce the ring case of the pic0 vanishing to LOCAL test rings (Zariski-local on Spec A), so the remaining obligation is at a local ring
summary=ADVANCED, NO GATE CLOSED (pic-g, 0096 r7). Released. Three files, rooted, 0 sorries, every declaration axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] vs a control (AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian) firing sorryAx. lake build EXIT=0.

(1) THE QUANTIFIER IS ZARISKI-LOCAL. Picard/Pic0RingZariskiLocal.lean. Both spellings of the surviving ring-case obligation reduce to a finite covering family of localizations, using only the SEPARATION half of the landed Zariski sheaf property (PicEtAff.eq_of_away_eq); nothing is glued. Then PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_forall_prime / rigidity_of_forall_prime remove the cover from the STATEMENT: a basic-open neighbourhood at each prime suffices, via Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite (compactness of Spec A). jacobianData_of_forall_prime_subsingleton and _rigidity compose that to the goal object, so the whole vanishing route now has a shortest form: a LOCAL computation of the plus construction at each prime of each test algebra, nothing else.

(2) THE DEGENERATE SITE IS SETTLED, and it went the opposite way to the fear. hrigAff antecedent is vacuous at a subsingleton test ring, which made it the cheapest potential refutation site (I-1655, recorded as unchecked). PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_subsingleton proves the CONCLUSION holds there anyway, unconditionally: Spec of a subsingleton ring is empty, so the product is, so CechPic and relPic are trivial, and every etale cover of a subsingleton ring is again subsingleton. So the affine spelling is SATISFIED at that site, not refuted.

(3) COMPUTING Pic ON A TWO-CHART COVER IS COMPUTING UNIT GROUPS. Picard/TwoChartCechPicTrivial.lean. The Wave-5 tangent lane built both halves of the two-chart comparison and never composed them; the composite turns a fact about the unit groups of THREE RINGS into triviality of a Picard class, general in the scheme.

(4) Pic(P1_A) = Z OVER A DOMAIN, both directions. Picard/LaurentTwoChartCoboundary.lean, mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_iff. AND the finding that runs against my own (3): not_tUnit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits shows the UNIVERSAL hypothesis of (3) is FALSE at P1 -- t is not a coboundary. Repaired in place by cechPic_eq_one_of_forall_presenting_coboundary, which constrains only the PRESENTING units and is a proved weakening. The obvious repair (the iff form) is VACUOUS and I shipped it first: the unused-variable linter flagged the chart-triviality hypothesis as doing no work.

THE RESIDUE, exactly, and it is NOT the quantifier any more: NO DEGREE MAP EXISTS on the two-chart Cech Picard group. Searched, absent. So "the class has degree zero" cannot yet be converted into "its presenting unit is C of a unit", which is the one bridge between the P1 computation and a real discharge of the ring case. That bridge is the next brick and it is pure bookkeeping compared with Traverso-Swan.

MEASURED, so nobody re-runs it: local does NOT imply seminormal. Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic A) IS available for local A (mathlib CommRing.Pic.instSubsingletonOfFiniteMaximalSpectrum) but Subsingleton (Pic (Polynomial A)) does NOT follow from IsLocalRing A -- exact? fails. Seminormality is absent from mathlib. So (1) moves the obligation to local rings and does not discharge it there.

=== AJCR.w4-rep.datum.vanishing-route
status=pending priority=normal owner=
title=NON-ATLAS INHABITANT of the pic0TypeFunctor representability slot, under testwise vanishing -- headline retracted from 'second route to JacobianData'
summary=CLAIMED pic-g (0096 r2). The three atlas antecedents (rep, IsChartUniv, coverage) are all antecedents of ONE route to JacobianData. This row builds a SECOND route needing none of them: if pic0Subgroup C T is trivial at every test T then pic0TypeFunctor C is represented by Over.mk (id (Spec k)), whose structure morphism is an iso, so locallyOfFiniteType and quasiCompact are FREE -- a JacobianData with no atlas, no divisor representability, no coverage. Then reduce the vanishing hypothesis from all tests to affine test RINGS, so it is attackable without scheme-level machinery. NO NEW HYPOTHESIS is added to any existing statement.

Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. the degree, pinned to the genus g by the functor.

Both directions come from one fibrewise reduction (ADDENDUM 4 §4.2).  For c in P^1(k) let W_c be
the image in Spec R of supp D meeting pi^{-1}(c); it is closed because supp D is finite over R,
and s in W_c iff the FIBRE supp(D_s) meets pi^{-1}(c).  Since D_s is finite of degree n over
kappa(s), its image in |P^1| has at most n closed points.
  IF: pick c in P^1(k) outside that image and any c' /= c; then Spec R minus W_c confines D to the
  chart complementary to pi^{-1}(c).  Doing this at every s gives a Zariski cover on which the
  divisor is confined, with the pair varying per member -- exactly what R1 allows.
  ONLY IF: if the sum over c in P^1(k) of e_c is at most n, where e_c is the minimal degree of a
  closed point of C over c, then a divisor of the form sum_c q_c + padding lies in W_c for EVERY
  c in P^1(k), and no pinned pair confines it.

CONSEQUENCES, and they decide the certificate route.
 * p1-aut is NOT dead.  It is correct over every infinite field, and over F_q whenever q >= g+1.
 * It cannot discharge the challenge on its own.  Challenge.lean:96-99 states the Jacobian over an
   ARBITRARY field and archon-protected.yaml forbids adding a hypothesis, so R1 must be paired
   with descent (dat-g) or replaced.
 * Of the three options this leaf was opened to choose between, (a) "accept |P^1(k)| >= n+2 as a
   hypothesis" is now known to be exactly the right hypothesis and exactly what the challenge
   forbids; (b) descent from a big enough k' is viable and is the pairing R1 needs; (c) degree-d
   closed points is unnecessary -- it is subsumed by R2, which is cleaner.
 * R2 is the only field-uniform fix and is no longer a gamble: supp D is finite over R, hence
   contained in a single affine open of C x_k Spec R (avoidance for families, Stacks 0B8B), so a
   cover with one straddling piece always exists.  Generalising FinCoverData's piece type to
   arbitrary affine opens of the relative curve is the statement the geometry already supports.

Related and settled the same round: the on-stratum witness the no-go lacked now exists at g >= 2
over any field (ADDENDUM 4 §4.3), so the no-go is not vacuous on the campaign's stratum; and
ADDENDUM 3's shrink-stability argument was the wrong criterion (a span-top cover cannot delete a
point) -- under the criterion it stated, the campaign's own genus-0 example would be evaded.
